summary: The gemeente proxy disaggregation method (estimated_births_gemeente = corop_births * stock_share_within_corop) injects a structural cross-sector correlation into gemeente-level velocity that is unrelated to any births precedence relationship. This inflates the Phase 7 sector-precedence regression results.

variance_decomposition.method: velocity variance split by COROP x year x sector group mean vs within-group residual

decomposition_regression.interpretation: share_velocity (the stock-share weighting term) has a coefficient ~10x larger than corop_velocity (the actual births signal), meaning small year-to-year fluctuations in a gemeente's stock share within its COROP dominate the proxy birth velocity, swamping the genuine COROP-level birth dynamics.

cross_sector_correlation_share_velocity.description: Pairwise correlation of stock_share velocity across A10 sectors within the same gemeente-year (the proxy WEIGHTING term, not births)
cross_sector_correlation_share_velocity.interpretation: Strong positive correlation across most sectors indicates a gemeente's general establishment-stock growth (gentrification, development) moves multiple sector stocks together, independent of any sector-to-sector births relationship.

cross_sector_correlation_proxy_births_ve.description: Pairwise correlation of estimated_births_gemeente velocity across A10 sectors (the actual Phase 7 regression input)
cross_sector_correlation_proxy_births_ve.comparison: Lower than share_velocity correlation but still elevated for sector pairs with high share_velocity correlation (e.g. GI-MN: 0.53), consistent with share_velocity being a major contributor to the births velocity signal.

consequence_for_phase7.interpretation: The ~15x jump in promoted edges (8 -> 121) when moving from COROP observed births to gemeente proxy births is not consistent with genuine sub-COROP signal discovery. It is consistent with the stock-share weighting term injecting artificial cross-sector co-movement that the permutation test treats as a births precedence signal. n_samples >= 60 and q_fdr < 0.05 are satisfied trivially because gemeente-year observations within the same COROP are not statistically independent: they share ~32.5% of velocity variance directly from the COROP-year-sector group, and the remaining within-group variance is itself ~67% driven by a stock-share term with structural cross-sector correlation up to 0.82.

recommendation: NL gemeente proxy Phase 7 sector-precedence edges (including the 97 nominally COVID-robust pairs) must NOT be used as training labels under any DEC-066 tier (ROBUST_ORIGINAL, FINE_GRAIN_SUPPORTED, or EXPLORATORY_FINE_GRAIN) until the regression is re-run with COROP-clustered standard errors / COROP fixed effects to absorb the shared stock-share component, or until an alternative proxy method is found that does not inject cross-sector stock co-movement into the births estimate.
